sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2018. A survey of word-level replacive tonal patterns in Western Mande. Mandenkan 59. doi:10.4000/mandenkan.1420
sources.note: Not about Mogofin: §4.1.2.1 (par. 62) 'There are four languages in the Mokole group: Kakabé, Kuranko, Lélé, and Mogofin.. little published data is available for Mogofin'; Kuranko (Kastenholz 1987) used as the Mokole exemplar. (OpenEdition PDF is behind an Anubis JS gate; read via the HTML page.)

sources.citation: Vydrine, Valentin. 2009. Esquisse de la langue lélé (groupe mokolé). Mandenkan 45: 29-104.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Lele, not Mogofin; group-level remark only: §3.3 (p. 42) 'Le système tonal lélé est typique des langues mandé et mokolé : deux registres; la déclinaison tonale (down-drift); deux classes tonales principales de mots.' Mogofin appears only in the lexicostatistical table (§2) and in the remark that Mogofin and Kakabe are phonologically and morphologically very close.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra & Valentin Vydrin. 2022. The Kakabe dialectal continuum: A lexicostatistical study. Language in Africa 3(1): 31-56. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2022-3-1-31-56
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. English version of the 2014 study; p. 35: 'The Mogofin data, given for external comparison, are drawn from (Polinder et al. 2009), and some missing terms were supplied by our field data' — the Mogofin column carries tone marks throughout; no prose on Mogofin prosody.

sources.citation: MERN (Mission évangélique réformée néerlandaise). 2020-2024. Alfabɛti Mɔgɔfin (Mogofin alphabet page) and site 'amarenkama.com' (language pages, numerals, proverbs, tales).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; 27-letter alphabet with sample sentences (a few acute accents in the samples, e.g. basilánu, bintanná, laborilá); no orthography statement on tone or accent; no grammar PDF on the site.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra. 2017. A corpus-based description of Kakabe, a Western Mande language: prosody in grammar. PhD thesis, INALCO (HAL tel-03203594).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing on Mogofin stress or tone. Mogofin is mentioned only as Kakabe's closest relative (p. 40: 'Kakabe and Mogofin are mutually-intellegible') and in the literature survey (p. 45: 'a M.A. thesis by Jacqueline Janse on Mogofin in Dutch (1999a) published also as a grammar sketch in French (Janse 1999b)'). Phonology chapters concern Kakabe only.

sources.citation: Vydrina, Alexandra & Valentin Vydrin. 2014. Предварительные наброски к диалектологии какабе [Preliminary sketches of Kakabe dialectology], pp. 229-251 (HAL halshs-00961389).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Table 1 gives a 100-item Swadesh list for Mogofin (from the authors' field notes and the MERN 'Lexique mɔgɔfin 2009') with lexical H/L tone marks on every word (e.g. bɛ́ɛ 'all', bùgùtá 'ashes', kóndéŋ-è 'bird'); p. 241 says the Mogofin data come from their own field records and the Lexique.

sources.citation: Polinder, Wim, Jacqueline Janse & Kees Jan van Linden. 2009-. Lexique / Dictionnaire Mɔgɔfin-Français. Garama (Boké): Mission Évangélique Réformée Néerlandaise — online Dictionary-App-Builder version, letters A and B.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No front matter, no prose on tone or stress. Entries carry a per-syllable tone string in slash notation (e.g. 'abada / / / adv jamais', 'adamadeŋɛ / \ \ / \ n homme', 'aligiyama \ \ \ / / n au-delà', 'ale \ \ PrPers lui'), i.e. the compilers treat Mogofin as a two-tone (H/L) language with lexically specified tone on every syllable.

sources.citation: Vydrine, Valentin. 1998. Sur l'écriture mandingue et mandé en caractères arabes (mandinka, bambara, soussou, mogofin). Mandenkan 33, 87 pp. Section 6 'L'adjami mogofin' (printed pp. 19-21) + 'Textes mogofin' (Texte 14, Alhousseyni Diallo).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sections 6.1-6.3 describe how consonants, vowels (a i u e/ɛ o/ɔ), vowel length and nasalisation are rendered in the Mogofin Arabic-script texts; the Mogofin texts are transcribed with tone marks, and fn. 55 says the tone/length notation is only preliminary. Vydrine also says a 'description préliminaire du mogofin' (with Mamadi Diane, IRLA Conakry, fieldwork April 1996) 'sera publiée prochainement'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Mixifore language' (en) and 'Mogofin' (fr); Wikidata Q3914478; Glottolog mixi1241 page.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; fr.wikipedia gives the MERN alphabet and cites Janse 1997/1999 and the MERN alphabet page; Glottolog lists only Janse 1999a/b and Kaba 1983 as descriptive sources.
